newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD only to know gold mine size end-1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD only to know gold mine size end-1997.

text.p: Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) will only have a report on reserves at its Serra Leste gold mine at the end of this year, a company official said.

"For practically most of last year, geological surveys were stopped. They are now starting again but we will only have a final report at the end of this year," said Helcio Guerra, manager of precious metals projects.

Soundings at Serra Leste in the northern state of Para were hit last year by protesting prospectors who claim they are entitled to some of the profits from the mine which CVRD announced could hold reserves of 150 tonnes.

The claims stem from the fact the mine is very close to Serra Pelada, the site of the biggest gold rush in history and where up to one million garimpeiros produced at their peak 90 of the country's 113 tonnes in 1988.
CVRD, backed by the law courts, has rejected the prospectors' claims.
In total the company has four surveys which are currently operating and a fifth will begin shortly, Guerra said.
After the discovery was made public in February last year, the company said it hoped to be in a better position to know the exact extent of the mines reserves by August last year.
CVRD is Brazil's largest gold producer and output reached just over 18 tonnes in 1996.
"Production this year should be around the same level," Guerra said.
The company hopes to increase production to 31 tonnes by the year 2000.
A strategic 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares is being sold at auction on April 29 for a minimum price of three billion reais ($2.83 billion).
